title: Starved Rock Country
seo_title: Starved Rock Country Adventure | Ottawa, IL
seo_description: Boating, kayaking, eBiking and outdoor fun in Starved Rock Country. Start on the Illinois River at Heritage Harbor in Ottawa, 90 minutes from Chicago.
body_html:
Those who have visited Starved Rock Country know it is the best place in northern Illinois for outdoor adventure, and historic Ottawa is the perfect jumping-off point. The natural, archaeological and historic character of the region lets you experience life along the riverbanks. From Ottawa to Starved Rock, all along the National Historic Scenic Byway down to Havana, you can enjoy the seasonal colors and rhythms of the forests, rivers, wetlands, bluffs and prairies that make Starved Rock Country unique.

Start on the Illinois River

Launch from premium boat ramps at Heritage Harbor Ottawa, about a mile from Quest's facility. You will find easy, uncrowded access to 12+ miles of beautiful, wide-open boating. Whether cruising or kayaking, make a day of the shoreline, sand beaches, rock cliffs (including Starved Rock and Buffalo Rock State Parks), hideaways and multiple food and beverage destinations.

Adventure for every season

From there the sky is the limit, literally. We are boaters, skiers and kayakers, of course, but just a few of the other adventures that await are skydiving, aircraft club and lessons, gliders, horseback riding, off-roading and ATV tracks, canoeing, white water rafting, paintball, fishing, archery, hunting, motorcycle riding, cross-country skiing, curling, ice skating, eagle and bird watching, and yoga. The list goes on.

You can also explore by electric bike on the I&M Canal Trail. Rent an eBike at Heritage Harbor or rent a kayak or paddleboard.

Close to everything, far from ordinary

Starved Rock Country is only ninety minutes from downtown Chicago (much less from many suburbs). You will not spend hours in a car trying to get away to your sanctuary, and you will not be too far away when it is time to head home. In Starved Rock Country you can explore outdoor Illinois while you discover yourself.

Consider this your personal invitation. Drop in anytime and we will be happy to guide you to the best spots along the river and throughout Starved Rock Country. See more at starvedrockcountry.com or on Facebook.

Boating on the Illinois River

Boating on the Illinois River is one of the Midwest's best-kept boating secrets. It is far less crowded than most lakes in northern Illinois, and the scenery is fantastic. Flowing through the heart of Starved Rock Country, it is the best way to see Starved Rock and Buffalo Rock State Parks and the natural bluffs that line the shore.

  • Plenty of room: Boat Club members can cruise the entire 13-mile "Ottawa Pool," from Marseilles Lock to Starved Rock Lock. No going in circles like on many lakes.
  • Free docking: members can dock free of charge at downtown Ottawa, with its restaurants and activities.
  • Places to hang out: "Bob's Beach" is one of several spots where boaters anchor to enjoy the surroundings and socialize. Islands along the river add scenery and side channels to explore.
  • Easy boating: even on a windy day with other boat traffic, the waves are rarely very high. Boating is almost always more comfortable than on a big lake, and tubing and skiing are possible just about any time.
  • No rush: no need to get up early to beat the traffic or wait until midweek to have your fun.

Read more in our Illinois River boating guide, or visit us in Ottawa.
